meta.prompt_suffix: Style: candid documentary photograph of a real place, not an advertisement, not CGI, not a composite. Shot on a full-frame camera with a 35mm lens at about f/2.8, standing eye level, available light only, true-to-life restrained colour, mild sensor noise, a slight handheld tilt, honest texture on skin, concrete, paper, painted steel and glass. Printed sheets and painted labels may clip a little but the overall image stays natural — never glowing, never hyper-saturated, no HDR look, no rim-light effects, no lens flare. NUMBER RULE: every Korean amount quoted in this prompt is printed on ONE unbroken line, never split in the middle of a digit group, and every character of the largest quoted line is at least one twelfth of the frame height so it still reads when the picture is shrunk to thumbnail size. LETTERING RULE: render only the Korean words and figures quoted in this prompt; every other sheet, notice, wall, board and sign in the frame is blank paper or printed too small and slightly out of focus to read — do not invent english text, latin letters, chinese characters, gibberish text, random lettering or invented words anywhere in the image. No title overlay text, no captions, no subtitle bars, no large lettering across the frame, no watermark, no graphic arrows, no highlight circles, no drawn charts and no overlaid panels.

thumbnails.concept_ko: 한 줄 메시지: 「담 하나를 사이에 두고 이미 두 세계로 갈려 있다」. 순자산 1억 원 미만이 29.5%(열 집 중 세 집)인데, 같은 프레임 담 너머 상위 0.1%의 커트라인은 97억 1,000만 원이다(verified-data 2절). ※ 금액 조합 교체 사유 — 40대·50대 중앙값(2억 8,384만/3억 1,685만)은 3,300만 원 차이라 「반지하 vs 초고층」으로 그리면 그림이 수치보다 앞서 과장이 된다. 100배 가까이 벌어지는 조합으로 바꿔야 좌우가 실제 숫자와 맞는다. [A 얼굴] 나 같은 사람(40대 월급쟁이 남성, 반지하 세대 앞) — 특수직업·다른세대·성공자 아님 [B 금액] "1억 원 미만" / "97억 1,000만 원" [C 사건] 벽보에서 손끝이 막 떨어지며 고개가 타워 쪽으로 돌아가는 중, 장바구니는 아직 다른 손에 매달려 있음 [D 주어] 담 이쪽 반지하 계단에 서 있는 게 나다 [구도] 좌우대비 — 좌: 반지하 창살·곰팡이 시멘트·계량기함 / 우: 롯데월드타워 시그니엘 서울과 유리 로비. 경계는 낡은 붉은 벽돌담의 수직 모서리(물리적 경계, 그래픽 분할선 없음). 글자를 전부 지워도 어느 쪽이 이긴 쪽인지 읽힌다 [텍스트] 제목「8층, 당신 자리는 몇 층입니까」 vs 썸네일「우리 나이대는 몇 층에서 멈춥니까」 — 층 개수가 아니라 멈추는 지점을 말한다
thumbnails.prompt_en: COMPOSITION RULE, HIGHEST PRIORITY: the photograph fills the entire 16:9 frame edge to edge with a real scene — never a letterbox band, never an empty panel, never a flat colour block, and never a large expanse of bare empty ground. The bottom three-eighths of the frame height is filled by the man's dark shoulder and the shadowed alley floor in front of the sunken window well, so deeply in shadow and so far out of focus that it reads as one single dark mass with no readable detail, which keeps overlay text legible on top of it. No face, no hand, no notice and no bright object sits in that bottom three-eighths — every face, hand, taped notice and printed board sits in the upper five-eighths, and the top of the brick wall, the taped notice and the standing estate board all cross the MIDDLE of the frame, never near the bottom edge. SCALE, EQUALLY IMPORTANT: the man in the grey zip-up jacket is the largest thing in the picture — his head and shoulders occupy the entire left third of the frame, his face alone spans roughly the top 55 to 60 percent of the frame height, the top of his hair touches the upper edge and is very slightly cropped by it, and his shoulder leaves the frame on the left. The people inside the bright lobby beyond the wall are far smaller, roughly one third of his head height. SCENE: TWO DIFFERENT WORLDS IN ONE FRAME, separated by a physical edge and nothing else. Photographed straight on from inside a narrow old residential alley in Seoul at standing eye level. The left side of the frame is the poor world the man belongs to — a sunken half-basement flat whose window sits at ankle height behind rusted steel bars, damp black mould streaking the bare cement, a dented gas meter box, a buckled steel gate, one bare fluorescent tube under the eave, bundled wiring stapled along the wall, cracked floor tiles, plastic buckets and a stack of flattened cardboard. Taped to that cement just to the right of the man, at mid frame height, a printed A4 notice carries one heavy black line reading "1억 원 미만" in Korean Hangul with a much smaller line under it reading "29.5%". A weathered red-brick boundary wall runs up the middle of the frame and its vertical corner is the only divider between the two halves. The right side of the frame is the rich world on the other side of that wall — Signiel Seoul in the Lotte World Tower rising in full above the low rooftops, its glass skin holding the last warm light of the evening, and at its foot a bright glass residential lobby. A large matte estate board stands on the pavement in front of that lobby and fills much of the right third at mid height, its top line reading "97억 1,000만 원" in tall black Korean characters with a smaller line beneath reading "상위 0.1%", every other row on it printed too small and slightly out of focus to read. Warm tungsten light leaks up out of the basement window well while cold blue evening light falls on the tower, and the two light sources meet along the brick corner. PEOPLE: the man in his forties has come down the alley toward his own door and stopped mid-step, one foot still on the sunken stair, his fingertips just lifting off the taped notice while his head turns up toward the tower — eyes wide open showing whites, mouth open, eyebrows pushed high, jaw slack, a plastic grocery bag still hanging from his other hand. Two small silhouettes cross the lit lobby beyond the wall without once looking his way.

SCENE: a long outdoor concrete staircase running up a steep old Korean hillside neighbourhood, photographed from the foot of the flight at standing eye level, looking straight up the climb. Four or five ordinary people in their thirties to fifties have stopped at different heights, spread out up the steps. White paint is stencilled across three of the risers, reading "30대", "40대" and "50대" in Korean Hangul from the lower steps upward. On the red-brick retaining wall beside the flight a large printed notice, as wide as the wall panel behind it, reads "1억 5,585만 원" in heavy black characters. Honest lived-in detail everywhere — cracked cement patches, a rusted water pipe, potted plants in styrofoam boxes, a bicycle chained to a post, laundry poles on a low roof, a stack of blank flyers curling under a stone. Soft late-afternoon light comes over the top of the hill. PEOPLE: the woman in her forties has stopped mid-climb with one foot still on the higher step, opening a folded A4 sheet whose crease is still standing up, her head just lifted from it — eyebrows raised, mouth slightly open, one hand gripping the paper edge. Behind and below her two men keep climbing with their heads down, one carrying a shopping bag, neither of them looking at her.

thumbnails.concept_ko: 한 줄 메시지: 「내 나이의 꼭대기 값이 이 숫자다」. 50대 상위 1% 커트라인 34억 5,000만 원(verified-data 2절)을 손에 든 종이로 얼굴 옆에 세워, 같은 상위 1%도 나이마다 값이 다르다는 이 편의 핵심 대비를 한 장으로 만든다. SCENE: a stairwell landing in an old Korean office building, photographed straight on at standing eye level. The man has just unfolded an A4 sheet and holds it up beside his own face, tilted flat toward the lens so that it fills the left third of the frame at mid height, while his other hand still presses the fold down. Thick handwritten marker on that sheet reads "34억 5,000만 원" in Korean Hangul right across the width of the page, with a much smaller line above it reading "50대 상위 1%". An A4 printout ruled into rows lies open on the table top at mid height, filling the left half of the frame; the row her fingertip is sliding along reads "32억 원" in heavy black print right across the width of the sheet, with a short label at the head of that row reading "40대" in Korean Hangul, while every other row on the sheet is printed too small and slightly out of focus to read. thumbnails.prompt_en: COMPOSITION RULE, HIGHEST PRIORITY: the photograph fills the entire 16:9 frame edge to edge with a real scene — never a letterbox band, never an empty panel, never a flat colour block, and never a large expanse of bare empty floor. The bottom three-eighths of the frame height is filled by the shadowed lowest steps and the dark out-of-focus backs of two people standing below the row, so deeply in shadow that it reads as one single dark mass with no readable detail, which keeps overlay text legible on top of it. No face, no hand, no notice and no bright object sits in that bottom three-eighths — all five people, every painted riser label and both wall notices sit in the upper five-eighths, and the run of steps crosses the MIDDLE of the frame, never near the bottom edge. SCALE, INHERITED FROM THE ANCHOR: five people stand in one unbroken row straight across the upper part of the frame, each one standing a single riser higher than the person to their left, so the line of heads climbs steadily from left to right; the man in his forties at the centre of the row is half a step nearer the camera and is the largest figure, his head spanning roughly the top third of the frame height, and the other four are noticeably smaller as the steps rise away from him. SCENE: the inside of a wide old Korean stairwell that steps up from left to right, photographed dead straight on at standing eye level so that all five people are seen frontally in a single line. White paint is stencilled on the five risers under their feet, reading "29세", "30대", "40대", "50대" and "60대" in Korean Hangul from left to right. On the left wall a large printed notice reads "13억 1,000만 원" in heavy black characters, and on the far right wall a second notice of the same size reads "44억 9,000만 원". The shaft is worn and real — flaking green wall paint, a red fire extinguisher, wiring stapled along the wall, a corkboard of blank curling sheets, a bucket left on a landing. Cool daylight comes through a tall dusty window on the right and cold fluorescent tubes burn along the ceiling. PEOPLE: none of them are still. On the far left a man in his late twenties grips his backpack strap and lifts a foot onto the next riser, mouth open, eyes wide. Next a woman in her thirties looks down at a folded sheet in her hand, eyebrows pulled together. At the centre the man in his forties has just raised his head toward the higher steps, eyes wide open showing whites and lips parted. Beyond him a woman in her fifties stands with folded arms looking back down the line, lips pressed tight. On the far right a man in his sixties is half turned away, already reaching for the door at the top.

SCENE: the same wide old Korean stairwell that steps up from left to right, photographed dead straight on at standing eye level, but this time from close in beside the man at the near end of the row. PEOPLE: the man in his forties wears a market apron over a work shirt, his fingertips just touching the stencilled label on the wall — eyes wide open showing whites, mouth open, eyebrows pushed high, the tendons standing out on his neck.
